BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Status:** Privileged advice – buyer-side only

## 0. Threshold point: the "pre-categorisation" and "FINAL" framing is rejected

Before the clause-by-clause, three framing devices in the Seller's cover material need to be put aside, consistent with playbook §0.4/6.3:

1. **"[STANDARD] … cleared by both sides … need no further scrutiny."** Nothing in our authority record shows any of these clauses were cleared by Wattlebridge. A counterparty cannot pre-clear our review. Every clause has been reviewed below regardless of label. Notably, the Seller marked *every* contentious liability clause [STANDARD] and left nothing [OPEN] – the effect, if accepted, would be to waive review of exactly the points we care most about.
2. **"Settled at principal level … marked FINAL."** We have no record of Amelia Frost (or any buyer principal) approving these positions. The Seller's assertion is not evidence of agreement. The reply should state expressly that the Buyer does not accept that any of these positions is agreed, final or cleared.
3. **"Market standard" preamble (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months, knowledge qualifiers).** Unverified assertion. Even if a position were common, that is not a reason to accept it against our mandate.

Also note the Seller's own Disclosure Letter §11 says "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included" – which contradicts the cover note's claim that the package is agreed. We should hold them to §11.

One further housekeeping point: the Disclosure Letter is dated **22 September 2026**; today is 5 November 2026. Several items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) are inherently time-sensitive. We should require a **refreshed disclosure letter and data-room cut-off** before signing and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

---

## 1. Clause-by-clause: departures from playbook

### 1.1 General warranty cap – cl 12.1 (Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m)
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m opening; 20% is a *conditional fallback* usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None given.
- **Analysis:** The Seller's number happens to coincide with our fallback. That is **not** clearance – a matching number does not satisfy the authority condition (§6.3 expressly). Accepting it now would also give away our fallback with nothing in return.
- **Push back:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is acceptable. If the deal team wants to move, obtain Amelia Frost's written approval referencing this specific draft first.

### 1.2 Thresholds – cl 12.2 (Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery)
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Analysis:** Three separate departures, each materially adverse: (i) de minimis 5× ours, (ii) basket 5× ours, (iii) the "excess only" (deductible) formulation versus our tipping basket. On a AUD 24m deal the Seller's structure means the first AUD 250,000 of loss is never recoverable, and individually small-but-real claims are disregarded entirely.
- **Push back:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping basket. The excess-only wording must be deleted; this is the single biggest hidden value shift in the threshold package.

### 1.3 Time limits – cl 12.3 / 13 (Seller: 18 months; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise")
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- **Analysis:** As with the cap, 18 months matches a fallback but is not authorised. More serious is the second sentence: a **default rule that every limitation sweeps across all Claims** unless carved out. That is a hidden general-regime override that would drag Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and completion-payment claims into the 18-month window and the general cap unless we spot and carve out each one. This directly conflicts with the playbook requirement to keep categories separate.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general warranties. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with the opposite default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties (Seller: same caps and time limits as general, "for administrative simplicity")
- **Playbook:** separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Analysis:** Unacceptable. If title to the shares fails we would be limited to AUD 4.8m (or whatever the general cap is) and 18 months, against a AUD 24m price. "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification. This item is non-negotiable in substance.
- **Push back:** Insist on a distinct Fundamental Warranty regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualifier.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance – cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Seller: apply to "all Claims of any nature")
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of *all* caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one on our side may waive this.
- **Analysis:** The Seller's draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**, and "all Claims of any nature" is drafted broadly enough to purport to cap and time-bar fraud and to exclude reliance on fraudulent statements. Enforceability aside, we cannot sign this. "All Claims of any nature" would also capture specific indemnities, completion-account/price adjustment claims and covenant breaches.
- **Push back:** Mandatory carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct across cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5. Confine the limitations to Warranty Claims; specific indemnities, Title, Tax, payment and covenant claims to sit outside.

### 1.6 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2 (Seller: whole data room DD-002 to DD-012 + statutory registers + public records)
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Analysis:** §1.1 is a classic whole-data-room general disclosure; §1.2 extends to public records. Combined with cl 8.3 (below), the practical effect is that nearly any matter discoverable anywhere is deemed disclosed and un-claimable. §1.4 (no admissions) is acceptable as boilerplate but should not be allowed to undercut the specific facts stated in §§2–10, which are useful to us.
- **Push back:** Delete §1.1 and §1.2 general disclosure. Replace with a "fairly disclosed" standard (sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter) tied to specific disclosures and specifically referenced documents only.

### 1.7 Buyer knowledge – cl 8.3 (Seller: no claim for anything Buyer or advisers knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records")
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Analysis:** This is the most aggressive formulation possible – actual *and constructive* knowledge, imputed from advisers, and extending to anything "discoverable". It would effectively convert the warranties into a nullity for any matter that was in the data room, and it would apply to Title given cl 12.3's "all Claims" default.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3 in its entirety. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be the *Seller's* awareness qualifier (named individuals, after due enquiry), not a buyer-knowledge bar.

### 1.8 Bluefen consent – cl 3 / 6.3 (Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied on delivery" of written consent)
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient.
- **Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue (DD-002) – this is the key commercial risk in the deal. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter §2 confirms that **no final written consent and no evidence of condition satisfaction** is in the data room. "Satisfied on delivery" means a conditional or qualified consent letter would satisfy the CP even if the 11.3 conditions were never met. Reasonable endeavours leaves the Seller free to walk away from an unsatisfied CP with no consequence.
- **Push back:** CP to require (i) unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 in agreed form, and (ii) evidence satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably) that each 11.3 condition is satisfied, in each case before Completion; Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours** with Buyer involvement in the approach to Bluefen. Consider a price/escrow consequence if consent slips.

### 1.9 Riverlark facility – cl 2 / 7 (Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion")
- **Playbook:** current payout figure, direct repayment out of Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking **plus** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Analysis:** Disclosure Letter §3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is in the data room. A post-completion release means we would pay AUD 24m for shares in a company whose assets remain encumbered to the bank, with no contractual hook on Riverlark. The "approximately" AUD 3.2m is a September figure; interest and fees will have moved it. Change-of-control cl 8.1 could also be triggered by Completion itself.
- **Push back:** Require (i) payout letter dated no earlier than 2 business days before Completion, (ii) repayment direct to Riverlark from Completion funds via the funds flow, (iii) executed deeds of release/PPSR discharges delivered at Completion. If Seller insists on post-Completion, we need an irrevocable bank undertaking in agreed form and Amelia Frost's sign-off – neither is currently available, so the default position is no.

### 1.10 Funds flow / DD-005 bonuses (Seller: AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller", not itemised)
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Analysis:** Disclosure Letter §5 confirms the bonuses are omitted from the funds flow and that on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax) are unaddressed. On a debt-free/cash-free deal, a Completion-triggered liability that crystallises in the Company post-Completion is effectively a buyer cost unless treated as Debt or funded by the Seller. Saying it is "a matter for the Seller" without a mechanism achieves nothing – the obligation sits in Paperbark, which we will own.
- **Push back:** Treat the AUD 420,000 plus superannuation, payroll tax and any other on-costs as a specific line item deducted from the price / paid from Seller proceeds at Completion (or expressly included in Debt). Request the bonus letters and a payroll calculation of on-costs.

### 1.11 Ironquay IP – cl 11.1 (Seller: indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "considered adequate")
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Analysis:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. Until then Paperbark may not own IP it is delivering to customers. The Disclosure Letter §4 is candid: AUD 180,000 shows as open on DD-010, there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. An indemnity capped at the payment amount does not cover the real exposures – customer claims, loss of use, cost of re-development, or Ironquay asserting ownership.
- **Push back:** (i) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure payment of the outstanding SOW3 fee and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a CP or Completion deliverable (this preserves the cure route); (ii) indemnity broadened to all loss arising from any defect in title to SOW3 Project Materials or any Ironquay claim, uncapped by reference to the fee, outside the general regime; (iii) we obtain independent verification of the AUD 180,000 (bank evidence or Ironquay statement) – we should not assume either payment or non-payment.

### 1.12 DD-006 export/privacy incident – cl 4.6 / Sch 6 (Seller: "preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material")
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Analysis:** The Disclosure Letter §6 is appropriately neutral and we should mirror that: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification status unknown as at 22 September. The Seller's cover-note characterisation "not expected to be material" is an opinion without supporting facts and is six weeks stale. We should not accept it, nor should we overstate the matter.
- **Push back:** (i) Seller covenant to preserve all logs and correspondence; (ii) complete the investigation and provide a written update (including any assessment of whether the Privacy Act notifiable data breach threshold is met) before signing and again before Completion; (iii) specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (uncapped by the general regime, or separately capped), and a warranty that the disclosure is complete and accurate as at the refreshed cut-off; (iv) no price adjustment proposed at this stage pending facts.

### 1.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (Seller: AUD 330,000 "ordinary-course operating costs")
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Analysis:** The Disclosure Letter §8 declines to say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course – so the Seller's cover note "ordinary course" assertion is not supported by its own disclosure. Three related AUD 110,000 renewals in DD-008/DD-011 read together may indicate a pre-committed spend profile rather than discretionary opex.
- **Push back:** Request the three contracts, renewal dates, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued or prepaid. Hold open the characterisation; determine Debt/working-capital treatment once facts are known. Do not concede "ordinary course" and do not yet demand a deduction.

### 1.14 Tax / IP ("settled under the general regime")
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution; keep categories separate.
- **Analysis:** The Seller is attempting, by assertion, to fold Tax and IP into the 20%/18-month/AUD 250k regime. We have not agreed this, and in combination with cl 12.3's "all Claims" default, it would be the consequence of silence.
- **Push back:** Mark Tax and IP expressly OPEN. Propose a separate tax indemnity/covenant and IP warranty regime with its own cap and period (to be negotiated), outside the general basket and knowledge qualifier. Do not propose unlimited liability.

### 1.15 Title ("evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012")
- **Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.
- **Analysis:** The Disclosure Letter §10 itself concedes DD-012 "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification". A seller-maintained register is not independent proof.
- **Push back:** Obtain ASIC company extract and historical extract, PPSR searches against Paperbark and Harbourglass, share certificates, board minutes/constitution confirming authority to transfer, and confirmation of no options/convertibles. Fundamental Warranties on title and capacity per §1.4 above.

### 1.16 Other disclosure items (lease DD-007; Mossvale DD-009)
- Both are stated neutrally and do not currently require pushback, but: confirm the DD-007 landlord **notification** is given at or before Completion (and check the lease for a change-of-control clause the disclosure may be under-describing); confirm DD-009 Mossvale's assignment restriction is not accompanied by a change-of-control trigger elsewhere in the contract. Request copies of both.

---

## 2. Cross-cutting observations

- **The Disclosure Letter helps us more than the cover note suggests.** §§2–5, 8 and 10 confirm, in the Seller's own words, that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay assignment, bonus funding and title verification are all outstanding, and that Sandbar's character is unstated. We should cite these admissions back in our mark-up and resist any attempt to withdraw them in a revised letter.
- **The interaction of cl 12.3 ("all Claims") + cl 8.3 (constructive knowledge) + Sch 7 (whole data room)** is the structural problem. Individually each is adverse; together they would mean that effectively any matter anywhere in the data room is disclosed, deemed known, and barred – across all categories including Title, Tax and IP. The reply should address them as a package and reject all three.
- **No fraud carve-out anywhere.** This alone should be flagged to Amelia Frost as a red-line item on first read.
- **Two numbers (20% cap, 18 months) coincide with our fallbacks.** Treat this as a reason for caution, not comfort. No authority has been given; we respond at our opening positions.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Framing | "[STANDARD]/FINAL/pre-cleared/market" | Reject expressly; all clauses reviewed; nothing agreed |
| 2 | General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m**; no fallback without Amelia Frost written authority |
| 3 | Thresholds (12.2) | AUD 25k / AUD 250k / excess only | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k / first-dollar** |
| 4 | Time limit (12.3/13) | 18 months; limits apply to all Claims by default | **24 months**; limits apply only to general Warranty Claims |
| 5 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **Separate regime: 100%, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar** |
| 6 | Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims | **Fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carved out everywhere**; indemnities, Tax, Title, payment and covenant claims outside |
| 7 | Disclosure (Sch 7, DL §1.1–1.2) | Whole data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only**; delete general disclosure |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Actual + constructive, incl. advisers | **Delete** |
| 9 | Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **Unconditional consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met, pre-Completion**; stronger endeavours |
| 10 | Riverlark (2/7) | Release post-Completion | **Current payout, direct repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion**; post-Completion only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval |
| 11 | DD-005 bonuses | Not in funds flow | **AUD 420k + on-costs as line item / Seller-funded / Debt** |
| 12 | Ironquay IP (11.1) | Limited to SOW3 payment | **Pay + confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; broadened indemnity**; verify AUD 180k independently |
| 13 | DD-006 incident (4.6/Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | **Preserve logs, complete investigation, refreshed written update, specific indemnity**; no numeric assumption |
| 14 | Sandbar renewals | "Ordinary course" | **Hold open; request contracts and terms**; no automatic Debt/deduction |
| 15 | Tax / IP | Folded into general regime | **Mark OPEN; separate regime to be negotiated**; no unlimited liability proposed |
| 16 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence**: ASIC extracts, PPSR, certificates, authority documents |
| 17 | Disclosure Letter date | 22 Sep 2026 | **Require refreshed letter and cut-off** before signing; preserve §§2–10 admissions |

**Immediate actions:** (a) brief Amelia Frost on the absence of any fraud carve-out, the Title/Fundamental collapse into the general regime, and the fact that no fallback authority exists for the 20%/18-month numbers; (b) issue a mark-up reinstating opening positions; (c) send a supplementary information request covering Bluefen, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment evidence, bonus letters and on-costs, Sandbar contracts, DD-006 update, lease and Mossvale contracts, and independent title searches.

I have not accepted any Seller characterisation ("required by law", "market", "agreed", "final", "pre-cleared") as a substantive instruction; where the Seller's cover note and its own Disclosure Letter conflict, I have relied on the disclosed facts and flagged the assertion.

Also note the Seller's own Disclosure Letter §11 says "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included" – which contradicts the cover note's claim that the package is agreed. We should hold them to §11.

One further housekeeping point: the Disclosure Letter is dated **22 September 2026**; today is 5 November 2026. Several items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) are inherently time-sensitive. We should require a **refreshed disclosure letter and data-room cut-off** before signing and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

## 1. Clause-by-clause: departures from playbook

### 1.1 General warranty cap – cl 12.1 (Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m)
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m opening; 20% is a *conditional fallback* usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None given.
- **Analysis:** The Seller's number happens to coincide with our fallback. That is **not** clearance – a matching number does not satisfy the authority condition (§6.3 expressly). Accepting it now would also give away our fallback with nothing in return.
- **Push back:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is acceptable. If the deal team wants to move, obtain Amelia Frost's written approval referencing this specific draft first.

### 1.2 Thresholds – cl 12.2 (Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery)
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Analysis:** Three separate departures, each materially adverse: (i) de minimis 5× ours, (ii) basket 5× ours, (iii) the "excess only" (deductible) formulation versus our tipping basket. On a AUD 24m deal the Seller's structure means the first AUD 250,000 of loss is never recoverable, and individually small-but-real claims are disregarded entirely.
- **Push back:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping basket. The excess-only wording must be deleted; this is the single biggest hidden value shift in the threshold package.

### 1.3 Time limits – cl 12.3 / 13 (Seller: 18 months; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise")
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- **Analysis:** As with the cap, 18 months matches a fallback but is not authorised. More serious is the second sentence: a **default rule that every limitation sweeps across all Claims** unless carved out. That is a hidden general-regime override that would drag Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and completion-payment claims into the 18-month window and the general cap unless we spot and carve out each one. This directly conflicts with the playbook requirement to keep categories separate.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general warranties. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with the opposite default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties (Seller: same caps and time limits as general, "for administrative simplicity")
- **Playbook:** separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Analysis:** Unacceptable. If title to the shares fails we would be limited to AUD 4.8m (or whatever the general cap is) and 18 months, against a AUD 24m price. "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification. This item is non-negotiable in substance.
- **Push back:** Insist on a distinct Fundamental Warranty regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualifier.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance – cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Seller: apply to "all Claims of any nature")
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of *all* caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one on our side may waive this.
- **Analysis:** The Seller's draft contains **no fraud carve-out at all**, and "all Claims of any nature" is drafted broadly enough to purport to cap and time-bar fraud and to exclude reliance on fraudulent statements. Enforceability aside, we cannot sign this. "All Claims of any nature" would also capture specific indemnities, completion-account/price adjustment claims and covenant breaches.
- **Push back:** Mandatory carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct across cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5. Confine the limitations to Warranty Claims; specific indemnities, Title, Tax, payment and covenant claims to sit outside.

### 1.6 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2 (Seller: whole data room DD-002 to DD-012 + statutory registers + public records)
- **Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Analysis:** §1.1 is a classic whole-data-room general disclosure; §1.2 extends to public records. Combined with cl 8.3 (below), the practical effect is that nearly any matter discoverable anywhere is deemed disclosed and un-claimable. §1.4 (no admissions) is acceptable as boilerplate but should not be allowed to undercut the specific facts stated in §§2–10, which are useful to us.
- **Push back:** Delete §1.1 and §1.2 general disclosure. Replace with a "fairly disclosed" standard (sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter) tied to specific disclosures and specifically referenced documents only.

### 1.7 Buyer knowledge – cl 8.3 (Seller: no claim for anything Buyer or advisers knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records")
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Analysis:** This is the most aggressive formulation possible – actual *and constructive* knowledge, imputed from advisers, and extending to anything "discoverable". It would effectively convert the warranties into a nullity for any matter that was in the data room, and it would apply to Title given cl 12.3's "all Claims" default.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3 in its entirety. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be the *Seller's* awareness qualifier (named individuals, after due enquiry), not a buyer-knowledge bar.

### 1.8 Bluefen consent – cl 3 / 6.3 (Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied on delivery" of written consent)
- **Playbook:** effective consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient.
- **Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue (DD-002) – this is the key commercial risk in the deal. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter §2 confirms that **no final written consent and no evidence of condition satisfaction** is in the data room. "Satisfied on delivery" means a conditional or qualified consent letter would satisfy the CP even if the 11.3 conditions were never met. Reasonable endeavours leaves the Seller free to walk away from an unsatisfied CP with no consequence.
- **Push back:** CP to require (i) unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 in agreed form, and (ii) evidence satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably) that each 11.3 condition is satisfied, in each case before Completion; Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours** with Buyer involvement in the approach to Bluefen. Consider a price/escrow consequence if consent slips.

### 1.9 Riverlark facility – cl 2 / 7 (Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion")
- **Playbook:** current payout figure, direct repayment out of Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking **plus** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Analysis:** Disclosure Letter §3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is in the data room. A post-completion release means we would pay AUD 24m for shares in a company whose assets remain encumbered to the bank, with no contractual hook on Riverlark. The "approximately" AUD 3.2m is a September figure; interest and fees will have moved it. Change-of-control cl 8.1 could also be triggered by Completion itself.
- **Push back:** Require (i) payout letter dated no earlier than 2 business days before Completion, (ii) repayment direct to Riverlark from Completion funds via the funds flow, (iii) executed deeds of release/PPSR discharges delivered at Completion. If Seller insists on post-Completion, we need an irrevocable bank undertaking in agreed form and Amelia Frost's sign-off – neither is currently available, so the default position is no.

### 1.10 Funds flow / DD-005 bonuses (Seller: AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller", not itemised)
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Analysis:** Disclosure Letter §5 confirms the bonuses are omitted from the funds flow and that on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax) are unaddressed. On a debt-free/cash-free deal, a Completion-triggered liability that crystallises in the Company post-Completion is effectively a buyer cost unless treated as Debt or funded by the Seller. Saying it is "a matter for the Seller" without a mechanism achieves nothing – the obligation sits in Paperbark, which we will own.
- **Push back:** Treat the AUD 420,000 plus superannuation, payroll tax and any other on-costs as a specific line item deducted from the price / paid from Seller proceeds at Completion (or expressly included in Debt). Request the bonus letters and a payroll calculation of on-costs.

### 1.11 Ironquay IP – cl 11.1 (Seller: indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "considered adequate")
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Analysis:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. Until then Paperbark may not own IP it is delivering to customers. The Disclosure Letter §4 is candid: AUD 180,000 shows as open on DD-010, there is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment. An indemnity capped at the payment amount does not cover the real exposures – customer claims, loss of use, cost of re-development, or Ironquay asserting ownership.
- **Push back:** (i) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure payment of the outstanding SOW3 fee and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a CP or Completion deliverable (this preserves the cure route); (ii) indemnity broadened to all loss arising from any defect in title to SOW3 Project Materials or any Ironquay claim, uncapped by reference to the fee, outside the general regime; (iii) we obtain independent verification of the AUD 180,000 (bank evidence or Ironquay statement) – we should not assume either payment or non-payment.

### 1.12 DD-006 export/privacy incident – cl 4.6 / Sch 6 (Seller: "preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material")
- **Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Analysis:** The Disclosure Letter §6 is appropriately neutral and we should mirror that: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification status unknown as at 22 September. The Seller's cover-note characterisation "not expected to be material" is an opinion without supporting facts and is six weeks stale. We should not accept it, nor should we overstate the matter.
- **Push back:** (i) Seller covenant to preserve all logs and correspondence; (ii) complete the investigation and provide a written update (including any assessment of whether the Privacy Act notifiable data breach threshold is met) before signing and again before Completion; (iii) specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (uncapped by the general regime, or separately capped), and a warranty that the disclosure is complete and accurate as at the refreshed cut-off; (iv) no price adjustment proposed at this stage pending facts.

### 1.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (Seller: AUD 330,000 "ordinary-course operating costs")
- **Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Analysis:** The Disclosure Letter §8 declines to say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course – so the Seller's cover note "ordinary course" assertion is not supported by its own disclosure. Three related AUD 110,000 renewals in DD-008/DD-011 read together may indicate a pre-committed spend profile rather than discretionary opex.
- **Push back:** Request the three contracts, renewal dates, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued or prepaid. Hold open the characterisation; determine Debt/working-capital treatment once facts are known. Do not concede "ordinary course" and do not yet demand a deduction.

### 1.14 Tax / IP ("settled under the general regime")
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution; keep categories separate.
- **Analysis:** The Seller is attempting, by assertion, to fold Tax and IP into the 20%/18-month/AUD 250k regime. We have not agreed this, and in combination with cl 12.3's "all Claims" default, it would be the consequence of silence.
- **Push back:** Mark Tax and IP expressly OPEN. Propose a separate tax indemnity/covenant and IP warranty regime with its own cap and period (to be negotiated), outside the general basket and knowledge qualifier. Do not propose unlimited liability.

### 1.15 Title ("evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012")
- **Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.
- **Analysis:** The Disclosure Letter §10 itself concedes DD-012 "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification". A seller-maintained register is not independent proof.
- **Push back:** Obtain ASIC company extract and historical extract, PPSR searches against Paperbark and Harbourglass, share certificates, board minutes/constitution confirming authority to transfer, and confirmation of no options/convertibles. Fundamental Warranties on title and capacity per §1.4 above.

### 1.16 Other disclosure items (lease DD-007; Mossvale DD-009)
- Both are stated neutrally and do not currently require pushback, but: confirm the DD-007 landlord **notification** is given at or before Completion (and check the lease for a change-of-control clause the disclosure may be under-describing); confirm DD-009 Mossvale's assignment restriction is not accompanied by a change-of-control trigger elsewhere in the contract. Request copies of both.

## 2. Cross-cutting observations

- **The Disclosure Letter helps us more than the cover note suggests.** §§2–5, 8 and 10 confirm, in the Seller's own words, that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay assignment, bonus funding and title verification are all outstanding, and that Sandbar's character is unstated. We should cite these admissions back in our mark-up and resist any attempt to withdraw them in a revised letter.
- **The interaction of cl 12.3 ("all Claims") + cl 8.3 (constructive knowledge) + Sch 7 (whole data room)** is the structural problem. Individually each is adverse; together they would mean that effectively any matter anywhere in the data room is disclosed, deemed known, and barred – across all categories including Title, Tax and IP. The reply should address them as a package and reject all three.
- **No fraud carve-out anywhere.** This alone should be flagged to Amelia Frost as a red-line item on first read.
- **Two numbers (20% cap, 18 months) coincide with our fallbacks.** Treat this as a reason for caution, not comfort. No authority has been given; we respond at our opening positions.
